name: Cross-stitch
basis: why: every stitch fills one square of the cloth grid; how: one pixel per square, floss palette, X as back and front strokes

lumenary.blurb: A sampler: your picture counted out in coloured thread, one X per square of the cloth, using a limited box of flosses.

facts.era: Centuries old, charted patterns from the 19th century
facts.bestOn: Bold, simple subjects with distinct colours

why: Cross-stitch is counting: the cloth is a grid of holes, and every stitch fills exactly one square. That makes the whole craft a pixel art problem. Shrink the picture to one pixel per square, limit the colours to a box of flosses and draw an X in each square, with back threads below and front threads on top for a woven look.
how: Shrink the picture to one pixel per square of cloth.
Find the k most representative colours with k-means, made slightly more saturated, and give each square the nearest.
Optionally leave squares lighter than 0.86 bare.
Draw the cloth with faint threads along every grid line and a dark hole at every corner.
Draw each stitch as two strokes: back strokes first in a slightly darker shade, then a soft shadow, then the front strokes with a thin pale highlight for the twist.
history: Counted thread embroidery has been worked for many centuries. Samplers, in which girls recorded stitches, alphabets and mottoes, were made from the sixteenth century onward, and printed charts of the nineteenth century, such as Berlin wool work, spread patterns widely. Today cross-stitch is a hobby for people who enjoy slow, careful making.
terms: A cloth woven with a grid of holes for counted embroidery.
Embroidery thread made of loosely twisted strands.
A piece of embroidery made to show off stitches or to record patterns.
paragraphs: Cross-stitch counts. The cloth (aida) is a grid of holes and every stitch fills one square, so the picture is first shrunk to one pixel per square, the “stitches across” slider. The colours are then limited to the box of flosses you chose: k-means clustering finds the k most representative colours of the small picture (made slightly more saturated) and each square takes the nearest one. The “bare” option skips squares lighter than 0.86, leaving the cloth showing.

Each stitch is a cross of two strokes drawn with round caps, inset from the corners of its square. All the back strokes (one diagonal) are drawn first in a slightly darker shade, then a soft offset shadow, then the front strokes in the true colour (the other diagonal), then a thin pale highlight along each front thread to suggest twist. The cloth itself is drawn first: faint threads along every grid line, and a small dark hole at every corner.

equations.note: Geometry of a stitch for n stitches across.
Each square takes the floss in the set F nearest to the average colour of its pixels; redmean is a distance that weights red and blue by brightness.

presets.text: A black cloth makes the colours glow.
Leave the light areas bare for a sampler look.
Fewer stitches across makes a chunkier, more graphic pattern.
